referenceData.instructions: Compare the next six-week support block for a fictional eight-year-old whose dyslexia and ADHD have already been professionally assessed. A positive classroom report can coexist with persistent decoding difficulty; renewing support on one overall success judgment could leave another need insufficiently addressed. Every response range is an authored assumption, not a validated prediction or a confidence interval. The classroom package is support for attention-related difficulties, not a complete clinical ADHD treatment. Separate progress measures inform reconsideration; before-and-after change alone does not establish a causal effect.
Prefilled values are fictional examples. Changing part of the workbook can leave example inputs in the case.
Edit the named input sheets. Keep worksheet names, column headers and record identifiers. Do not add formulas. Other case inputs remain unchanged.

All response assumptions refer to the fictional six-week support horizon. Reading uses additional correct items on a declared 20-item probe; participation uses percentage-point change under a declared observation protocol; additional burden is minutes per week. No monetary conversion or probability is inferred. Null response bounds remain unknown. Sources, applicability, goals and priorities require qualified human judgment.
